title: Versailles
objective: After this level you can describe Versailles and its Hall of Mirrors.
summary: Louis XIV turned a hunting lodge into an immense palace that from 1682 held the whole court, keeping nobles under his eye. Its Hall of Mirrors (1678-84) boasted 357 mirrors when mirrors were a luxury.

cards.headline: Versailles started as a hunting lodge.
cards.body: It was built for Louis XIII in the 1620s. His son Louis XIV transformed it, between 1661 and 1710, into an immense palace. Why would a king need that much house?

cards.headline: Room for everyone who mattered
cards.body: From 1682 Versailles was the official royal residence, with room to house the whole court. That was the point. Under the king's watchful eye, the nobility could no longer plot against the throne; the great lords were kept eager to serve and please him. The best way to watch your rivals is to invite them to move in.

mascot.line: A palace big enough for every rival. Very generous. Very watchful.

cards.headline: The Hall of Mirrors
cards.body: Jules Hardouin-Mansart built it from 1678 to 1684, replacing an open terrace onto the garden. The gallery runs more than 70 metres, with 17 arches of mirrors facing 17 windows: 357 mirrors in all. Overhead, Charles Le Brun's 30 ceiling paintings tell the story of Louis XIV's reign. Guess who's the hero.

cards.fact: A wall of mirrors was a wall of money.
cards.context: At the time, mirrors were a great luxury, and Venice held a monopoly on making them. This hall showed that France's new mirror manufacture could rival Venice. Courtiers crossed it daily, so every walk to work was a small advertisement.
